findings.title: ATTEMPT_NOT_PAYABLE classified as NO_MONEY, but one return site fires after a verified capture
findings.where: design.md §3.1 set membership, §3.2, §3.3 NO_MONEY branch, §12 (no row); order_creation.py post-capture may_create_order branch
findings.problem: reconcile_payment returns ATTEMPT_NOT_PAYABLE both before the provider call (unsupported checkoutMode) and after paid+amount+currency all matched. The design maps it to NO_MONEY: 200, lease closed, one INFO line, no PAID_BUT_NO_ORDER alarm, no recovery row. A captured payment therefore produces zero paid orders with no durable record and no provider retry.
findings.fix: Split into ATTEMPT_NOT_PAYABLE (pre-verification only, NO_MONEY) and a new PAID_BUT_NOT_ELIGIBLE in PAID_BUT_BLOCKED_OUTCOMES and PERMANENT_OUTCOMES; make the pre-verification checkoutMode refusal verify first or classify TRANSIENT so an unverified capture never closes the lease; add §12 rows and test_a_verified_capture_that_fails_eligibility_is_paid_but_blocked.

findings.title: Event-supplied notes.purpose still selects the subject; two financial branches precede the restructured block and one leaves no record
findings.where: design.md §3.3 ("no financial side effect is lexically reachable without a materialized order"), §7, §5.2; handler.py wallet_topup and secure_file_download early returns
findings.problem: Both early branches are above the restructured block and return. A genuine commerce capture carrying purpose: wallet_topup lands as a wallet STRUCTURAL recovery row and never reaches commerce reconciliation (the sweep only re-runs the top-up path for a top-up), so zero paid orders permanently. purpose: secure_file_download returns after a fire-and-forget invoke with no recovery row at all. The lexical-unreachability claim is false as written.
findings.fix: Resolve the subject from server state only (PAYREF#, TOPUPINTENT#/TOPUPLINK#, invoice referenceId-index with provenance, secure-files grant); refuse on zero or more than one stored subject with a recovery row; demote notes.purpose to a logged hint with a subject_hint_disagree corroboration line; pin with test_notes_purpose_cannot_route_a_commerce_capture_away_from_commerce and test_a_capture_with_no_stored_subject_always_leaves_a_recovery_row.

findings.title: Inbound-WhatsApp authorize() names no server-stored expected amount, making obligation 4 self-referential
findings.problem: expected_amount_paise and expected_currency are unspecified for the whatsapp_meta call. The only amount in scope in _process_payment_status is actual_amount, derived from the inbound webhook, so the amount obligation would compare the event against itself while gating _mark_invoice_paid_by_reference, the order_status send, GST document generation and the balance-due notification.
findings.fix: Pass the stored invoice amount: resolve exactly one invoice for the reference and use money.positive_paise(invoice['amountPaise']) with expected_currency='INR'; if amountPaise is not stored on those rows, add it to the producer in the same change rather than deriving from the editable display total. Add test_the_whatsapp_path_compares_against_the_stored_invoice_amount.

findings.title: Legacy path's permanent refusals are specified as raise CaptureUnresolved, which is the transport's TRANSIENT signal
findings.problem: CaptureUnresolved means retry (500, lease open) in the transport and never-retry (PERMANENT) inside the legacy path. Only one can hold. On the first reading a permanently unbindable legacy capture retries forever, reintroducing audit §4.3 on the legacy branch, and whether a recovery row is written is unstated for the raising paths. HIGH-2 and MEDIUM-2 both funnel genuine commerce captures into this branch.
findings.fix: Make the legacy path return a verdict instead of raising: _legacy_verdict() then always _record_unresolved() before any return, return on PERMANENT (200, lease closed), raise CaptureUnresolved only on TRANSIENT. Add LEGACY_BINDING_ABSENT, LEGACY_INVOICE_AMBIGUOUS and LEGACY_NOTES_DISAGREE to PERMANENT_OUTCOMES with §12 rows, and state in CaptureUnresolved's docstring that it means TRANSIENT only.

findings.title: The named test suite cannot run: FakeDynamo rejects every condition shape the design is built from
findings.problem: The fake raises AssertionError on any ' OR ', understands only attribute_exists/attribute_not_exists/X = :v joined by AND and raises on any other fragment (so <=, <, >= and contains are hard errors), supports ADD of a numeric placeholder only (no string sets), and exposes no transact_write_items. _stage, record_paid, binding_condition_expression, recovery's stateRank guards, lease() CAS, credit_topup_once and §7.1's two-Put transaction all depend on those forms. With no deploy and no live verification, these tests are the entire evidence base.
findings.fix: Add a step 0 to §18 extending the fake: OR with parenthesised precedence, <, <=, >, >= against numeric placeholders, contains/NOT contains over sets and strings, string-set ADD, and a FakeClient.transact_write_items with per-item conditions and TransactionCanceledException carrying CancellationReasons. Acceptance: tests/test_fake_dynamo_grammar.py asserts each new form refuses what real DynamoDB refuses and that an unparsed fragment still raises. Explicitly reject the alternative of asserting on expression strings.

findings.title: credit_topup_once reports a never-credited top-up as success
findings.problem: ConditionExpression combines attribute_exists(wabaId) with the appliedTopups set check, and DynamoDB does not report which arm failed. A verified capture against a missing wallet row returns {credited: False} = success, the recovery row is RESOLVED, and the money is never credited or flagged. The design also drops partner_billing.topup's ensure_wallet call and its status = ACTIVE write, so a suspended wallet paying to un-suspend stays suspended.
findings.fix: Call ensure_wallet first; on ConditionalCheckFailedException re-read with ConsistentRead and distinguish: wallet missing -> raise WalletMissing (TRANSIENT, recovery row stays open); idempotency_key present in appliedTopups -> idempotent success; anything else -> raise. Keep SET #s = :active in the UpdateExpression. Add test_a_credit_against_a_missing_wallet_is_never_reported_as_credited and test_a_verified_topup_reactivates_a_suspended_wallet.

findings.title: Outcome enumeration is not a partition and disposition() is not total over what the handler returns
findings.problem: NOT_A_COMMERCE_REFERENCE (the outcome that unlocks the legacy branch) is in no *_OUTCOMES set; RECONCILIATION_ERROR is a raw handler string, not a constant, and is in no set so disposition() would raise on it despite the stated totality test naming it; NO_PROVIDER_ID is returned early with no disposition key, so §3.3's verdict.get('disposition') is None, matches no branch, and reaches raise CaptureUnresolved with no classification -> retried forever on an event that can never acquire a provider id.
findings.fix: Introduce ALL_OUTCOMES as the single source; promote RECONCILIATION_ERROR (TRANSIENT) and NO_PROVIDER_ID (PERMANENT) to constants; assert disposition is total over ALL_OUTCOMES and that PERMANENT_OUTCOMES | TRANSIENT_OUTCOMES == PAID_BUT_BLOCKED_OUTCOMES exactly; AST-assert that every dict return in _create_order_for_captured_payment carries a disposition key.

findings.title: load_attempt's two-valued contract cannot express the NOT_A_COMMERCE_REFERENCE vs UNKNOWN_REFERENCE split
findings.where: design.md §3.1 and its claim about closing audit §4.2; handler.py _load_attempt
findings.problem: _load_attempt returns None both when no PAYREF row exists and when a row exists but carries no paymentAttemptId, so the design's distinction is unreachable and the second case still routes a commerce reference to the legacy branch. (order_keys._read_row does use ConsistentRead=True, so lag is not the cause; a lost or half-written row is.)
findings.fix: Add AttemptBindingUnusable; return None only for a confirmed-absent PAYREF row, raise AttemptBindingUnusable when the row exists but names no usable attempt; catch it in reconcile_payment before the generic except and map to UNKNOWN_REFERENCE (paid-but-blocked, PERMANENT). Pin with test_a_payref_row_without_an_attempt_is_never_treated_as_legacy.

findings.title: Verifier selector rewrite would GET /payments/<order id> on the normal checkout path
findings.problem: target is both the /payments/<id> path segment and the identity the returned payment must equal. 'The selector is bound_payment or bound_order' sends a Razorpay order id to the payments endpoint whenever providerPaymentId is absent, which §4.2 says is the normal Standard Checkout case, producing a 404 -> PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE -> TRANSIENT on every real capture. It also contradicts §4.4's own branch structure.
findings.fix: Keep two distinct selectors: require bound_order (else RazorpayBindingMissing); if bound_payment is non-empty read /payments/<bound_payment>, otherwise read /orders/<bound_order>/payments; match the event's payment_id only inside the server-selected set and never place it in a URL. Add test_an_attempt_with_no_bound_payment_id_is_verified_through_the_order_endpoint.

findings.title: providerAmountPaise creates a second authoritative amount with no stated relation to attempt.amountPaise
findings.where: design.md §4.2, §4.3, §4.4 point 3 versus order_creation's comparison against attempt['amountPaise']
findings.problem: Two stored amounts for one payment with no rule that they agree, no assertion at the seam, and no statement of which is authoritative; finalization writes attempt['amountPaise'] onto the order row.
findings.fix: Add AND amountPaise = :amt to bind_gateway_order's ConditionExpression so a divergent binding cannot be stored, and add to §14: attempt.amountPaise is the single authoritative total and providerAmountPaise may only ever equal it. Test test_binding_a_different_amount_than_the_attempt_is_refused.

findings.title: providerMode has no named source on the verification side, and the obvious one is secret-derived
findings.problem: 'payment liveness' names no response field. The natural substitute is key_id.startswith('rzp_live_'), which is secret-derived and collides with §11.3 and with this repository's two CodeQL py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data failures on values reduced from a secret. No fallback is specified when the field is absent, unlike account_id's U-3. The API read is already mode-scoped by the credential used.
findings.fix: Preferred: state that mode is enforced structurally by the credential, keep providerMode on the binding as provenance only, and remove it from the compared obligations with a comment saying why. If it must be compared, name the exact response field, extend U-3's degradation rule to it, and state that the derived mode must never appear in a logging expression, not even as a bool.

findings.title: side_effect_guard effect names do not add up and the legacy/WhatsApp effects have no members in the closed set
findings.where: design.md §2 (two new effects), §9.4 (three), §6 (six guarded effects), §5.3 (four); side_effect_guard.KNOWN_EFFECTS
findings.problem: Count disagreement between §2 and §9.4; NOTIFICATION duplicates the existing CONFIRMATION so one business action gets two marker keys; and _store_payment_record, _mark_invoice_paid_by_reference, _post_payment_handler, _log_ctwa_purchase, the order_status send and _trigger_post_payment_flow have no members in KNOWN_EFFECTS, so _validate raises ValueError after the claim is taken -> 500 with an open lease on an authorised payment.
findings.fix: Enumerate all nine effects in one edit (reuse CONFIRMATION, drop NOTIFICATION, add CART_COMPLETION, PAYMENT_RECORD, INVOICE_PAID, GST_DOCUMENT, META_PURCHASE, POST_PAYMENT_FLOW, WALLET_CREDIT), correct the count in §2/§9.4, and state the subject-key convention for non-order subjects (LEGACY_INVOICE#<id>, TOPUPINTENT#<id>) or rename claim()'s order_id parameter to subject_key and update existing callers and tests/test_side_effect_guard.py in the same step.

findings.title: accept_paid rewrite drops the purchased-snapshot precondition
findings.where: design.md §9.4 pseudocode versus the current finalization.accept_paid; §9.1 still lists PURCHASED_SNAPSHOT_MISSING
findings.problem: The current code parks before writing the order row when purchasedSnapshot or snapshotHash is absent. The rewrite omits that check while still building the order from attempt['purchasedSnapshot'] and attempt['snapshotHash'], so a paid attempt without a snapshot raises KeyError instead of parking, or commits an internal order with no immutable purchased snapshot.
findings.fix: Reinstate the gate between PAYMENT_VERIFIED and the order write, parking with _park('PURCHASED_SNAPSHOT_MISSING') and retaining paid state. Test test_a_paid_attempt_with_no_snapshot_parks_and_writes_no_order_row.

findings.title: Extending the AST gate to in (...) finds a second live offender the design does not mention
findings.problem: After extending the walk to ast.In/ast.NotIn there are two offenders across CONSULTING_FILES, not one: invoice-engine/handler.py:766 and inbound-whatsapp-handler/handler.py:3943 (inv_ps not in ('captured','paid','refunded')), which selects which other invoices are still unpaid and misses authorized and disputed. 'Full suite green' cannot hold at step 11 as written.
findings.fix: Add the second site to §11.2 and to the owned paths, rewritten as pay_status.rank(inv_ps) < pay_status.STATUS_RANK[pay_status.CAPTURED], and run the extended gate against all existing CONSULTING_FILES before adding the three new entries so the blast radius is known up front.

findings.title: Recovery sweep's replay inputs are unspecified and its only pointer to the event is a TTL'd row
findings.problem: _create_order_for_captured_payment takes a Razorpay payment entity dict and the design never says how the sweep reconstructs it; the only stored route back to the event is webhook_log_id into RazorpayWebhookLogTable, which has a 180-day TTL while the recovery row deliberately has none, silently bounding 'still recoverable after acknowledgment'; and dedupKey in recoveryId = '<channel>#<dedupKey>' is never defined, so two event types describing one capture may produce two rows.
findings.fix: Key recoveryId on the payment (channel#subjectKind#providerPaymentId-or-providerOrderId); have record() store the minimal replay inputs (providerPaymentId, providerOrderId, referenceId, channel, subjectKind, subjectId) and have the sweep rebuild {'id':..., 'order_id':...} from the row and re-read the provider, never the log row and never the stored amount; keep webhook_log_id as a non-load-bearing pointer. Test test_the_sweep_replays_from_the_recovery_row_alone with the log table emptied.

findings.title: §7.1's own conversion truncates the fractional paise the same paragraph says it rejects
findings.problem: int(Decimal(str(body['amount'])) * 100) truncates: Decimal('100.555') * 100 -> 10055.5 -> 10055, silently discarding half a paise, directly contradicting 'A fractional-paise amount is rejected with 400, not rounded'. The int() launders the value before money.positive_paise (which refuses a non-integral Decimal) can catch it.
findings.fix: paise = Decimal(str(body['amount'])) * 100; reject with 400 when paise != paise.to_integral_value(); then amount_paise = money.positive_paise(paise). Test test_a_fractional_paise_topup_is_rejected_not_rounded with '100.555'.

findings.title: Float inventory is incomplete, so §11.1 overstates the remaining surface
findings.problem: partner-onboarding has two float(body.get('amount') or 0) sites. The design fixes _do_topup_order at :587 and does not mention _do_topup at :427, the admin credit, which passes the float into billing.topup -> _dec(amount). §11.1 reads as a complete inventory of live float money inputs and is not one.
findings.fix: Either validate the admin input through the same boundary (Decimal(str(...)) plus an integral-paise check, keeping topup()'s signature) or amend §11.1 to record the fourth site explicitly as out of scope with its reason. Silence is the only wrong option.

findings.title: The credit's audit row goes into a TTL'd table and changes that table's sort key
findings.problem: PartnerLedger rows carry ttl = now + LEDGER_TTL_DAYS * 86400 (default 400), so the only record of what a real money credit was for expires, in a design that disables TTL elsewhere for exactly this reason. Separately the table's sort key is ts (ISO timestamp) and every reader and the _ledger writer assume it; writing TOPUP#<intentId> into it changes ledger ordering semantics with no statement about readers.
findings.fix: Keep ts as the sort key, carry intentId as a plain attribute, express once-only via a separate uniqueness row if wanted, and write the durable provenance where it cannot expire: onto the TOPUPINTENT# row (creditedAt, creditedAmountPaise, providerPaymentId) and onto the recovery row at resolve(). State that PartnerLedger is a 400-day operational view, not the audit record.

findings.title: PON-5 stale-comment list is short by one site and its line numbers have drifted
findings.problem: Stale sites are :28 (module docstring, omitted from the list), :164, :422 (cited as :415) and :546 (cited as :530). Three other '12-character' occurrences are correct descriptions of the legacy form.
findings.fix: Fix all four and re-derive the line numbers at edit time.

findings.title: Baseline HEAD and the dirty-path ownership map are already stale
findings.problem: HEAD is 25eace20, not 43b26d4a, and git status now also shows scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py, four src/** files and tests/test_legacy_redirect_rollback_snapshot.py as modified plus new untracked docs/execution and tests files, none owned by this task. The index is still clean, so the substance of §0 holds.
findings.fix: Re-derive the ownership map and git status --short immediately before step 1, keep git commit --only on named paths per U-9, and leave the src/** and url-host-routing changes alone.

findings.title: Two incompatible verify contracts are never reconciled in text
findings.problem: capture_authority.authorize's verify returns a provider record dict; reconcile_payment's verify_payment returns a 4-tuple. Both are correct for their callers, but §5.2's 'delegates obligations 3 and 4 to capture_authority.status_is_captured / amounts_match' is unactionable without saying which module performs which.
findings.fix: State that obligation 3 is performed inside razorpay_verify (which owns the provider record), obligation 4 inside order_creation (which owns the authoritative amount), and authorize() is used by the three non-commerce channels only.

findings.title: money is edited at step 1 but absent from the owned-paths list and the module map
findings.problem: Step 1 names money contract additions, but lambda_utils/ecommerce/money.py appears in neither the owned-paths list nor the module map. The path is ecommerce/money.py; lambda_utils/money.py does not exist.
findings.fix: Add the full path to the owned-paths list, or state that money is used unchanged (which matches §11.1, since positive_paise already refuses bool, non-integral Decimal, non-int, <= 0 and > 2**53-1).

findings.title: No gate ties the live alias move to the seam having a caller
findings.problem: BINDING_MISSING is the expected state for every real capture until the checkout workstream calls bind_gateway_order, and that state closes the dedup lease, so deploying before the caller exists converts 'provider keeps retrying' into 'provider gave up, a human owns it'.
findings.fix: Add to §18: do not publish a version or move the live alias until bind_gateway_order has a caller, or until the owner accepts paid-and-blocked captures in writing.
